title: Pre-baked gradient texture vs live gradient + clip-path
variable: baked texture vs linear-gradient with clip-path
claim: Angled gradient-filled shapes (ability slots, faction banners, skewed HUD panels) are the classic 'should this be CSS or a sprite?' decision. Unlike box-shadow-baked, this comparison can be pixel-faithful, so the ratio is a clean read on what a live gradient plus clip-path costs against a texture blit.
result: CONFIRMED, and one of the largest effects in the lab: Paint 2.26x / 5.12x / 15.09x, GPU 1.62x and 2.02x at the upper counts, RecordRendering 7.71x / 8.55x / 8.99x. A live linear-gradient plus clip-path costs fifteen times the paint of the same artwork as a texture at 300 elements. Note what this does NOT say: gradient-radial-vs-linear and gradient-conic-vs-linear both found the gradient FUNCTION free to choose. It is having a live gradient at all, not which one, that costs - and baking recovers it.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. linear-gradient is supported (feature inventory: css-function partial - the ONE restriction is that two-position 'double stop' shorthand such as 'red 0 10px' is rejected, which this case avoids by using a plain two-stop gradient). clip-path is supported for polygon() (css/partial.json rejects only fill-box, path, stroke-box and view-box; polygon is listed as a supported css-function). url() verified manually - see box-shadow-baked notes. Rule 1: one variable, how the shape is produced. Rule 2: identical DOM and identical 88x64 geometry - unlike a box-shadow, clip-path clips INSIDE the border box, so the texture reproduces it exactly and no geometry exception is needed. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte. Rule 4 EXCEPTION: A loads gradient-clip-baked.png, B loads nothing - the asset IS the variable. Generated by tools/make-baked-images.js from the same gradient stops and the same polygon, so the two variants are pixel-faithful by construction. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: shared root-nudge damage driver. Rule 7: no randomness. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is GPU.
